$doc: POS parity classification map — evidence-backed status per docs/pos-parity-matrix.md row. Stream P2 domains: customers (27), shift (28), cash (5), invoices (21), returns (15) = 96 matrix rows / 94 unique slugs (invoice-void + invoice-return appear in both invoices and returns). Statuses: covered = verified React implementation + named test; not-required = matrix-documented dead/orphan/negative finding or structurally-obsolete legacy mechanics with quoted reason; unclassified = genuinely missing and genuinely required — left open on purpose. Tests marked '(wave-1: B2)' are placeholders for components announced by the parallel build-streams; the coordinator replaces them with real test refs at merge.

cust-history-no-detail.reason: Matrix-documented NEGATIVE finding (a gap in legacy, not a feature): «NONE — rows are not clickable … rows are rendered as plain <tr>, no onclick/data-action». Nothing existed to port.

cust-checkout-outcome-toast.reason: Structurally obsolete. Legacy created/linked the ERP customer as a SIDE EFFECT of checkout and had to report customerSaveOutcome afterwards (app.js:2680-2702: 'linked-existing / created-new / skipped-no-phone / failed-insert…'). React links a REAL customerId at cart time via CustomerPicker (O2C), so there is no save-outcome to report post-sale — failures surface at pick/create time instead, before money moves.

React uses closing-data-v3, whose response has NO items array (lib/types.ts ClosingDataV3), and ShiftDialog renders no items table — genuinely missing, needs either the v1 endpoint or items added to v3.

shift-close-reveal-gate.gap: Legacy blind-count control: expected totals stay hidden until the cashier checks «أنهيت العدّ» (app.js:5815-5827). React ShiftDialog shows expectedAmount per method WHILE counting — the anti-fraud gate is genuinely missing, not obsolete.

shift-close-variance-note-gate.gap: Legacy refuses to close on a variance until a ≥10-char explanation is typed (app.js:5767-5776, 5829-5837). React's ملاحظات الإغلاق is optional and never gates the close — genuinely missing control.

shift-close-button-lock-unlock.gap: Legacy locks the confirm button until counting is finished / variance explained (_scLockClose/_scUnlockClose). React's تأكيد إغلاق الوردية is always enabled — missing together with the reveal/variance gates (rows 6 & 8); the three form one blind-count control.

shift-report-whatsapp.gap: Legacy shares the shift report via wa.me (app.js:2872-2922). No React equivalent and not announced by any build-stream — genuinely missing convenience feature; product may also choose to drop it, but that is a product call, not a classification.

shift-variance-modal-orphan.reason: Matrix-documented DEAD CODE: «NONE — grep across public/pos/app.js finds zero references to '#modalShiftVariance' or '#varianceBody'. Never [invoked]» — orphan markup, nothing to port.

shift-quick-actions-menu-desktop.reason: Structurally obsolete. The collapsible #floatActions popover (toggled by clicking the 'POS' nav link) existed to bolt cashier actions onto the legacy shared header. React's purpose-built header (Header.tsx) exposes the same actions — shift chip/close, فواتيري, sync report — as first-class always-visible controls; there is no hidden menu to port.

shift-quick-actions-mobile-drawer.reason: Structurally obsolete. Legacy injected an 'إجراءات الكاشير' box into the hamburger drawer on <768px (app.js:4340-4456) because the shared header could not show POS actions on mobile. React's header is responsive (flex-wrap) and the same actions stay directly reachable on mobile.

shift-menu-auto-dismiss.reason: Dismissal mechanics (Escape/inside-click/outside-click) of the #floatActions menu — a menu that does not exist in React because its actions are inline in the header. Mechanics of a nonexistent surface.

shift-menu-swipe-and-autocollapse.reason: Swipe-to-show/hide + 5-second auto-collapse of the same nonexistent #floatActions menu (app.js:4461-4485). Nothing to port.

shift-nav-mobile-relocation.reason: Matrix: «No UI — invisible layout repair» — a MutationObserver hack (_moveAppNavToBody) that relocated the legacy shared header's nav out of the header on mobile. React renders its own layout; the defect the hack repaired does not exist.

Under ORDER_TO_CASH_ENABLE=1 the POS void/return path is 409-gated (middleware/o2cLegacyGate) and reversals carry O2C's far stronger confirmation chain (draft→approve→post with separation of duties, salesReturns.api.test.js); non-privileged POS actions still confirm through ManagerApprovalDialog.
shift-my-invoices-confirm-modal.notes: Residual UX nit if the O2C flag were OFF: a privileged (admin/manager) إلغاء fires with no confirm step. Recorded in the stream report.

cart-footer-keyboard-access.reason: Structurally obsolete. The legacy «document keydown listener» (app.js:1944-1951) compensated for a non-semantic div role=button cart footer. The React pay control is a native <button> (CartPanel.tsx pay action, plus the F4 shortcut in App.tsx) — keyboard operability comes from the platform, no listener to port.
